Contamination-aware differential expression

Source: vignettes/contamination-aware-de.Rmd
contamination-aware-de.Rmd

The problem

In a case/control single-cell study, samples differ in how much ambient RNA they carry. Fragile disease tissue lyses more, so its soup is larger and is enriched for the disease genes of whichever cell type is abundant. Those reads land in every droplet. A pseudobulk test on a rare cell type then reports the abundant type’s disease genes as differentially expressed in the rare type.

ambient_de() does not subtract the soup. It puts each sample’s measured soup inside the model as a known additive term:

ygs∼NB(Nsexp⁡(xs⊤βg)+ρsTssoupgs)y_{gs} \sim \mathrm{NB}\big(N_s \exp(x_s^\top \beta_g) + \rho_s T_s\,\mathrm{soup}_{gs}\big)

and tests βg\beta_g with a quasi-likelihood F-test.

A simulated study with known truth

simulate_ambient_study() makes 6 control and 6 disease samples. Cell type A is abundant and has 80 disease genes. Cell type R is rare and has 40 disease genes of its own. Disease samples carry about 12% ambient RNA, controls about 5%.

library(Decant)
st <- simulate_ambient_study(seed = 3, G = 600, n_cells = 500)
table(st$cond)
#> 
#> ctrl  dis 
#>    6    6
round(tapply(st$rho_true, st$cond, mean), 3)
#>  ctrl   dis 
#> 0.052 0.111

Pseudobulk the rare type, one column per sample:

is_R <- st$label == "R"
samples <- sort(unique(st$sample))
Y <- vapply(samples, function(s)
  rowSums(st$X[, is_R & st$sample == s, drop = FALSE]), numeric(nrow(st$X)))
rownames(Y) <- rownames(st$X)
dim(Y)
#> [1] 600  12

Run the test

empties is a list with one empty-droplet matrix per sample, in the same order as the columns of Y.

design <- model.matrix(~ st$cond)
res <- ambient_de(Y, st$empties, design)
head(res[, c("gene", "logFC", "PValue", "FDR", "ambient_frac", "naive_FDR", "ambient_driven")])
#>     gene     logFC       PValue          FDR ambient_frac    naive_FDR
#> 117 g218  1.462029 2.746077e-10 8.952210e-08   0.02752370 2.085851e-07
#> 173 g309  1.222120 6.475971e-09 1.055583e-06   0.01134446 7.910796e-06
#> 189 g338  1.183664 3.708674e-08 4.030093e-06   0.01707288 7.910796e-06
#> 84  g158 -1.092676 1.740945e-07 1.418870e-05   0.01294913 1.077668e-05
#> 99  g184 -1.182222 4.557539e-07 2.971515e-05   0.01613194 7.910796e-06
#> 47  g121 -1.033911 6.203022e-07 3.069116e-05   0.01149664 1.295151e-05
#>     ambient_driven
#> 117          FALSE
#> 173          FALSE
#> 189          FALSE
#> 84           FALSE
#> 99           FALSE
#> 47           FALSE

naive_FDR is standard edgeR on the same pseudobulk. ambient_driven marks genes that edgeR calls and the contamination-aware test does not.

Score against the truth 

gi <- as.integer(sub("g", "", res$gene))
leaked <- gi %in% st$de_abund   # A's disease genes: any call in R is false
true_de <- gi %in% st$de_rare   # R's own disease genes
c(leaked_called_naive  = sum(res$naive_FDR[leaked] < 0.1),
  leaked_called_decant = sum(res$FDR[leaked] < 0.1),
  power_naive  = mean(res$naive_FDR[true_de] < 0.1),
  power_decant = mean(res$FDR[true_de] < 0.1))
#>  leaked_called_naive leaked_called_decant          power_naive 
#>            0.0000000            0.0000000            0.8333333 
#>         power_decant 
#>            0.8611111

On a Seurat object

DecantDE() does the pseudobulking and reads each donor’s raw matrix:

res <- DecantDE(obj, cell_type = "Microglia", sample_col = "donor",
                formula = ~ diagnosis, raw = raw_paths_by_donor)
subset(res, ambient_driven)

What this does not show

  • The simulator is built around the additive-soup mechanism the test assumes. This vignette shows the method does what it is designed to do. It is not real-data evidence.
  • Correcting counts first and then testing is not always worse. In validation/de_comparators.R, official SoupX followed by edgeR removes almost all leakage on this simulator, at some cost in power. See the README for the table.
  • With very few empty droplets, or three samples per group, the test leaks or loses power. The README lists the measured limits.
